title: Diego Hurtado de Mendoza to Ferrante Gonzaga, Siena, 3 April 1549 (catalogue 2161): cipher enclosure c. 44r read in part, key rebuilt from the contemporary decipherment on c. 42r and tested on held-out lines

documents.shelfmark: Biblioteca Estense Universitaria, Modena, Autografoteca Campori, Lettera H, Hurtado de Mendoza, Diego, sfasc. I, cc. 40-46 (cipher c. 44r; decipherment c. 42r)
documents.route: Diego Hurtado de Mendoza, Siena -> Ferrante Gonzaga, Milan

plaintext.source: c. 42r, a contemporary decipherment of c. 44r laid over it in the binding (identified by Brice Dudout, issue #254). It departs from the cipher in four places (NOTES.md).

transcription.source: Estense Digital Library IIIF region tiles, c. 44r stitched at full resolution (5426 px)
transcription.notes: Two passes from different crops (four bands 1:1, five bands 1.2x), reconciled on the image; 378 signs, 95 distinct sign names; the 30 points are not counted in tokens. Some near shapes not yet split (NOTES.md, Remaining gaps).

system.summary: Spanish chancery syllabary of the mendoza1548 family: consonant shapes with vowel marks, single letters, joined forms, a doubling dash, points, and code groups chu (tiempo), dis (emperador), qre (vuestra).
system.notes: One null sign, the point, in 30 places (a null or word mark); nulls.count is the number of null signs. distinct_symbols counts our 95 sign names, points aside (key.tsv has 96 entries: the 95 names and the point); some names probably merge two near shapes. Code groups: 3 distinct, 4 occurrences.

prior_solution.where: c. 42r of the same file, the contemporary decipherment. Dudout's alignment of 340/376 signs (issue #254, PR #265 closed) is not in the repository. No print found (web search 12 Nov 2026; Vazquez and Rose, Yale 1935, which the catalogue status line dates 1945, and Varo Zafra 2016 not opened).

conditions.human_role: WAINUT set the task (catalogue 2161) and the rules; AI language-model agents transcribed, aligned, froze the key, read and checked; one further AI language-model agent reviewed the reading blind (13 Nov 2026). No human palaeographer checked the text.
tools: scripts in this folder (tile fetch, line crops, key build, mechanical decryption, held-out test, mark check)
models: AI language-model agents (WAINUT), viewing the images

solution.what: cc. 42r and 44r stitched from IIIF region tiles (whole-image requests refused with 422).
Repository, issues and PRs for 2161, Mendoza, Gonzaga, Campori; one web search: no edition, no prior decipherment beyond c. 42r itself.
c. 44r transcribed twice from different crops by shape names written before any key; differences settled on the image.
Every sign aligned with c. 42r (align_44r.txt); key_frozen.tsv from lines L01-L10.

Frozen key on held-out lines L11-L17 (147 signs): 91/147 (61.9%) give the value read; 91/115 (79.1%) of the signs the frozen key knows; 99/115 (86.1%) same consonant. The held-out plaintext was in view during transcription.
Decrypted with key.tsv and read with every departure marked; scripts/check_marks.py passes. 154 words: 122 verbatim, 4 code, 28 repaired, 0 holes.

Independent blind review: sign spot-check of 4 lines (92 signs and 8 points) against the image, same segmentation, name differences only in marks and near shapes; key_frozen.tsv rebuilt from L01-L10 with the same 74 entries; reading read as sentences against the translation, grade B. The marked block moved out of reading_44r.md into reading_44r_marked.md.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 405 tokens, 96 types, es-golden-age order 4: reading -2.078 per letter; random keys -3.587 (z 8.9); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.218 (mean -2.264, z 5.2); annealer on the real text -2.13. Verdict: pass.

Integration check (13 Nov 2026): check_marks.py and heldout.py re-run (122 of 154 words verbatim; frozen key 91 of 147 held-out signs, 79.1% of the 115 known); c. 44r re-fetched from the IIIF tiles and lines 1-3 compared with the transcription (line structure, word breaks and about 35 signs agree). Strict share 79.2% (code words count as holes); read in part. The held-out test is a within-page consistency test, not a test on a second text. Gaps (shape splits, struck passages on cc. 40v/41r/46v, key of mendoza1548 not tried) are workable, so the target stays in progress and has no page.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -1.905; polyphony 0.086; 3 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.13

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: Key rebuilt by aligning c. 44r with its contemporary decipherment on c. 42r, frozen on lines 1-10 and tested on lines 11-17.
outcome.fraction_read_source: reading_44r_marked.md: 122 of 154 words verbatim from the signs (scripts/reading.py check). 22 of those 122 hold a sign whose value rests on that one place, taken from the alignment with c. 42r alone; without them 100 of 154 (64.9%).

texts.label: c. 44r, cipher enclosure on the government of Siena
texts.summary: Mendoza explains how the voting rules for the Eight and a Captain of the People decide whether Siena stays a republic, becomes a principate of the few or a duchy like Florence; he made the captain for four months the first time to test how the brigata (probably the faction) would bear it, asks Ferrante to keep this from the court lest they say one of them wants to make himself tyrant, and says he has deceived Juan Gallego so that the Emperor is left with the door open to enter with an appearance of reason.
texts.note: Words 154: 122 verbatim from the signs (79.2%), 4 code-group words, 28 with a marked single-sign repair, 0 holes. 22 of the 122 verbatim words hold a sign whose value rests on that one place (from c. 42r alone); without them 100 of 154 (64.9%). Marked reading line by line in reading_44r_marked.md.

reading_review.note: Read as sentences against translation_44r.md: all 12 sentences build, with no holes; a sign spot-check of 4 lines (92 signs and 8 points) against the image gave the same segmentation, with name differences only in marks. 28 words carry a single-sign repair from the contemporary decipherment on c. 42r, and several sign values rest on that crib alone, so the state is read in part.

gaps.item: Shape splits: x (de/no), o' (ga/ta), n (a/co/c/f), lo (mo/tro), q' (ha/a), 9 (do/u), e (lo/le)
gaps.detail: Probably two near shapes merged in each name; most of the 28 repairs sit here. A third look at 3x crops should split them.

gaps.item: Three signs unexplained in place: o in Florencia, p in vez, S in Juan
gaps.detail: Each name occurs once or twice on the page.
22 of the 122 verbatim words hold a sign whose value is attested in one place only and comes from c. 42r alone; without them 100 of 154 words (64.9%).
